HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. PAINTED INTRO-CARD. WORM’S-EYE from the black water, HARD DUTCH. ONE DEVICE: the aisle as a pale painted seam racing to the mouth. FOREGROUND: Sadaham’s FACE HUGE at the left edge — ice-blue silk, crescent headband, LEFT sheet face copied exactly, looking down-aisle not at us. Midground receding on the left bank: Mugwan steel-blue (SECOND), Gwisan green (THIRD). Right bank receding: Chuhang (FOURTH), Bangul (FIFTH), Gwanchang (SIXTH) — six different men, never clones. Munmu a tiny winter-coat speck in the mouth, NO crown in the ranks. Jewel colour: ice-blue, green, white-silk catching lamp, steam blooming #6fa8ff into the wash at one edge. Faces inked, cavern PAINTED watercolor-and-oil, paper grain. Only six hwarang plus the speck. No front lineup. No text. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = sadaham, SECOND face = mugwan, THIRD face = gwisan, FOURTH face = chuhang, FIFTH face = bangul, SIXTH face = gwanchang, #7 face = munmu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. SADAHAM — Look: Young hwarang: long black hair, defined jaw, ice-blue po, magenta sash, crescent headband. Same age as the river-stone and roof stills — a young man, not a child. Colour #6fa8ff. MUGWAN — Look: Young hwarang: long black hair, quieter defined face, cream po with a dusty-rose collar and sash, crescent headband. Same age as Sadaham in the river-stone stills — a young man, not a child. Colour #7aa0c8. GWISAN — Look: Young Hwarang: smooth Korean face, a small confident smirk, red liner at the outer eye, black hair under a cyan crescent-moon headband. Dress: Leaf-green po over dark wrapped forearms, brown sash, small jougwan with two tan pheasant feathers (attached /ch_gwisan.png). Colour #3d8c4a. CHUHANG — Look: Young Hwarang: longer wavy brown-black hair, a lazy half-smile, red around the eyes, a hint of stubble. Softer than Gwisan, not less decided. Dress: Slate-blue po over dark sleeves, teal crescent-moon headband with a dark swirl, teal sash tails, small jougwan with two tan pheasant feathers (attached /ch_chuhang.png). Colour #4a7a8c. BANGUL — Look: Boy of fifteen at the Yellow Mountain: square Korean face, a bright reckless half-grin, red liner at the outer eye, long black hair; crimson crescent-moon headband with long red tails. Dress: White hwarang po over a sky-blue inner collar, crimson sash tails, dark under-sleeves, small jougwan with two tan pheasant feathers (attached /ch_bangul.png). Colour #5e9dd8. GWANCHANG — Look: Boy of fifteen at the Yellow Mountain: smooth face, bright eyes with a red liner wing, long black hair in a topknot with side locks; Silla-blue headband with a crescent-moon emblem. Dress: White hwarang po with crimson collar and crimson sash, dark under-sleeves, wrapped forearms. Colour #79b6f2. KING MUNMU — Look: Square jaw, goatee and moustache, confident grin; arms folded when he is pleased with himself. Dress: As king: crimson robe with gold dragon embroidery, blue shoulder pieces, gold Silla crown. Earlier: prince/hwarang stage portraits. Crown: Silla gold crown exactly as the attached museum photo (Cheonmachong / Hwangnamdaechong, 27 to 36 cm tall, as tall again as the face): an OPEN crown with no cap or lining, the hair and topknot showing through it. A NARROW flat gold headband (about a thumb wide) sits level on the forehead. Rising from it, THREE flat sheet-gold tree uprights, one at the centre front and one over each ear: each is a straight vertical stem whose short straight side-branches turn UP at right angles in three or four stacked tiers (like 出), every tip a small bud or heart. At the BACK, two shorter flat antler-shaped uprights angle outward with alternating branches, seen behind the tree uprights, never curling out like horns at the sides. Every upright and the band is hung on fine gold wires with hundreds of small round trembling gold spangles and many curved pale-green jade gogok. From the band at each temple, a long pendant chain of gold leaf-shapes falls past the cheek to the collarbone. Thin, bright, pale gold-silver sheet that trembles and catches light. NEVER a solid basket, never a castle battlement or fence, never horns or deer antlers curving at the sides, never a cap inside, never a European spiked crown or tiara. Colour #C41E3A. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
